_readme: Example only (a made-up restaurant). Copy to the project's private discovery/ folder, keep only the questions the homework left open, and rewrite the options from what the research found. Same ids in a text or call version keep the answers comparable.
title: A few questions before we design
intro: Five minutes, no wrong answers. We looked at your site and your Instagram, so these are only the decisions we can't make without you.

questions.decides: who the first screen speaks to
questions.prompt: Who do you most want to reach with the new site?

options.label: Families looking for a weekend meal
People who work nearby, at lunch
People planning a party or catering
Our regulars, so they come back more

questions.prompt: What should a visitor do first?

options.label: Book a table or an event

questions.help: Pick the one that would make a stranger walk in.

options.label: How long we've been here and what people say

questions.decides: what the site can show as proof
questions.prompt: What can we show? Only what you already have.

options.label: Real photos of our food and place
Google or Yelp reviews we can quote
How many years we've been open

questions.prompt: Which two words should describe how the site feels?

questions.decides: what to take from a site they like
questions.prompt: You mentioned a restaurant site you like. What do you like about it?

options.label: What it says about the place
The reviews or awards it shows
How easy it is to order or book

questions.prompt: Anything we must keep, avoid or never say?

conflicts.message: Simple and lively pull in different directions; ask which one wins on the first screen.
They want to lead with credibility but have no proof yet; ask what they can share, or lead with something else.
